title: Foreign browser requests can consume authentication-protected one-time secrets using a victim session
summary: A holder of a secret link ID without an account can induce a signed-in visitor to consume an authentication-protected one-time secret or file through forged browser navigation; sibling-origin requests can also use cookie authority for authenticated creation. The fix ignores cookie authority for foreign origins and browser GET navigation while retaining configured split-origin frontends and non-browser clients. It does not claim that the link holder learns plaintext, keys, or session cookies.
ai_role: The Yopass maintainer's case-specific security advisory explicitly credits Anthropic's OSS Scanner as discoverer (tracking identifier ANT-2026-YEZ39BJO). It does not name a model version or internal discovery date.
classification_note: The public maintainer advisory documents the finding; it does not establish whether defenders knew of it or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: Yopass 16.0.0 fixes the issue (commit 8058174d6a04e23344433f5f07b23c320c1c5184). Affected-version scope: Affected versions 14.0.0 through 15.1.0; fixed in 16.0.0. Intentional frontend auto-retrieval with prefetch-secret=false and clients without browser-origin metadata remain outside the stated protection. Patch availability does not establish downstream deployment.

impacts.conditions: Unauthorized cross-origin browser activity can consume a protected one-time secret/file using a visitor’s session; this describes consumption, not plaintext disclosure to the link holder.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes a possible or reproducible trigger as stated; it does not report observed exploitation in the wild.
